summary.text: Ned Lamont is the incumbent Democratic Governor of Connecticut, seeking a third term with Lt. Gov. Susan Bysiewicz. A businessman who founded the cable-services company Campus Televideo, he won the governorship in 2018 and was re-elected in 2022. His campaign emphasizes lowering costs, universal pre-K and child care, housing supply and energy-cost oversight of utilities.

paragraphs.text: Lamont was born in Washington, D.C.
He earned a B.A. from Harvard College in 1976 and an M.B.A. from the Yale School of Management in 1980.
Lamont founded Campus Televideo, a cable and satellite services company for college campuses, and also founded a weekly newspaper.
He served as a Greenwich selectman from 1987 to 1989, and later on the Greenwich Board of Estimate and Taxation, and chaired the State Investment Advisory Council.
Lamont won the 2006 Democratic U.S. Senate primary against Joe Lieberman, but lost that year's Senate race to Lieberman, and he lost the 2010 Democratic gubernatorial primary.
He won the governorship in 2018 and 2022, taking office on January 9, 2019, and beginning a second term on January 4, 2023.
